title: Candy Distribution
description: There are n children standing in a line, each assigned a rating value given in the array ratings. You are giving candies to these children subject to the following requirements: each child must have at least one candy, and children with a higher rating get more candies than their neighbors. Return the minimum number of candies you need to have to distribute the candies to the children.
constraints: Each child must receive at least one candy

examples.explanation: You can allocate candies as [2, 1, 2], totaling 5, satisfying all constraints.
You can allocate candies as [1, 2, 1], totaling 4. The third child gets 1 candy, satisfying the constraint since it's not strictly greater than the second child.

title: Minimum Number of Taps to Water a Garden
description: There is a one-dimensional garden on the x-axis with points from 0 to n. There are n + 1 taps located at points [0, 1, ..., n] in the garden. Given an integer n and an integer array ranges of length n + 1 where ranges[i] means the ith tap can water the area [i - ranges[i], i + ranges[i]] if it was open. Return the minimum number of taps that should be open to water the whole garden, or -1 if the garden cannot be watered.
constraints: The garden spans from point 0 to point n

examples.explanation: Opening tap 0 covers the range [-3,3], but tap 0 actually covers up to [0-3,0+3], so opening just tap 1 (which covers [-3,5]) is sufficient, requiring only 1 tap.
Every tap has a range of 0, so none of the garden can be watered.

title: Create Maximum Number from Two Arrays
description: You are given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of lengths m and n respectively, containing digits 0-9 representing two numbers without leading zeros. You are also given an integer k. Create the maximum number of length k <= m + n from digits of the two numbers, preserving the relative order of digits from the same array. Return an array of the k digits representing the answer.
constraints: 0 <= nums1[i], nums2[i] <= 9, and 1 <= k <= m + n

examples.explanation: The maximum number of length 5 formed by merging digits while preserving relative order from each array is 98653.
Using all digits from both arrays in the order that maximizes the result yields 67604.

title: Video Stitching
description: You are given a series of video clips from a sporting event that lasted t seconds. These video clips can be overlapping with each other and have varying lengths. Each video clip is described by an array clips where clips[i] = [starti, endi] indicates that the ith clip started at starti and ended at endi. Return the minimum number of clips needed so that you can cut the clips into segments that cover the entire sporting event [0, t]. If it is impossible, return -1.
constraints: The clips together must cover the interval from 0 to t if possible

examples.explanation: Using clips [0,2], [1,9], and [8,10] covers the entire range [0,10] with the minimum number of clips.
The given clips only cover the interval [0,2], which is not enough to cover [0,5].

title: Minimum Cost to Hire K Workers
description: There are n workers, where the ith worker has a quality[i] and a minimum wage expectation wage[i]. We want to hire exactly k workers to form a paid group, following the rules: every worker in the paid group must be paid at least their minimum wage expectation, and in the group, each worker's pay must be directly proportional to their quality compared to other workers in the group, meaning if a worker's quality is double that of another worker in the group, they must be paid twice as much. Return the least amount of money needed to form a paid group satisfying these rules, expressed as a string rounded to 5 decimal places.
constraints: The group must consist of exactly k workers

examples.explanation: Hiring workers 0 and 2 gives a ratio of 7 per unit quality (based on worker 0), costing 10*7 + 5*7 = 105.
Selecting the optimal group of 3 workers based on the ratio approach yields a minimum cost of approximately 30.66667.
